intro.say: Some of the time it is day, and some of the time it is night. Let's see what is different!

rounds.say: In the day, the Sun shines in the sky. It is light, and we can play outside.
rounds.caption: day

rounds.say: At night, it is dark. We may see the Moon and stars. It is time to sleep.
rounds.caption: night

rounds.ask: The sky is dark and you see stars. Is it day or night?

options.label: day
options.why: In the day, the sky is bright from the Sun.

rounds.explain: At night the sky is dark, so we can see stars.

rounds.ask: Do we do this in the day or at night?
rounds.explain: We play in the bright day and sleep at night. Owls like me wake up at night!

rounds.ask: What gives us light in the day?

options.label: the Moon
options.why: The Moon shines at night. The Sun lights up the day.

options.label: a lamp
options.why: Lamps help at night. In the day, the Sun gives light.

rounds.explain: The Sun is very bright and lights up the day.

rounds.ask: What do you see in the sky at night?

options.label: rainbow
options.why: Rainbows need sunshine. At night we see the Moon.

rounds.explain: We often see the Moon and stars at night.

intro.say: The Sun and the Moon are both in our sky. Let's find out how they are different.

rounds.say: The Sun is a star! It is a giant ball of hot glowing gas. It gives us light and keeps us warm.
rounds.caption: The Sun is a star

rounds.say: The Moon does not make its own light. It shines because sunlight bounces off it, like a mirror.
rounds.caption: The Moon reflects sunlight

rounds.ask: The Sun is a kind of what?

options.label: planet
options.why: Earth is a planet. The Sun is a star.

options.label: cloud
options.why: Clouds are in our sky. The Sun is a huge star.

rounds.explain: The Sun is a star, the closest star to us.

rounds.ask: What does the Sun give us?

options.label: rain and snow
options.why: Rain comes from clouds. The Sun gives light and heat.

rounds.explain: The Sun gives us light to see and heat to keep us warm.

options.label: it is on fire
options.why: The Moon is not burning. Sunlight bounces off it.

options.label: it has lights
options.why: There are no lamps on the Moon. It reflects sunlight.

rounds.explain: The Moon reflects light from the Sun.

rounds.ask: Is it safe to look straight at the Sun?

options.label: yes, for a long time
options.why: The Sun is so bright it can hurt your eyes. Never look at it.

rounds.explain: The Sun is so bright it can hurt your eyes, so never look straight at it.

intro.say: Our Earth is always moving! It spins around and around, and it travels around the Sun.

rounds.say: Earth spins like a top. When our side faces the Sun, it is day. When it faces away, it is night.
rounds.caption: Earth spins: day and night

rounds.say: One spin takes one whole day. Earth also travels all the way around the Sun. That trip takes one year.
rounds.caption: 1 spin = 1 day · 1 trip = 1 year

rounds.say: The Moon changes shape in our sky. We see different amounts of its sunny side as it goes around Earth.
rounds.caption: Moon shapes

rounds.ask: Why do we have day and night?

options.label: the Sun turns off
options.why: The Sun always shines. Our side of Earth turns away from it.

options.label: clouds cover the Sun
options.why: Clouds can't make night. Earth spinning does.

rounds.explain: Earth spins, so our side faces the Sun for day and turns away for night.

rounds.ask: How long does Earth take to go all the way around the Sun?

options.label: one day
options.why: One day is one spin. Going around the Sun takes a year.

options.label: one week
options.why: It takes much longer, one whole year.

rounds.explain: Earth takes one whole year to travel around the Sun.

rounds.ask: Put the Moon shapes in order, from new Moon to full Moon.
rounds.explain: The sunny side we see grows bigger each night until it is a full Moon.

rounds.ask: Your side of Earth faces away from the Sun. Is it day or night?

options.label: day
options.why: Day is when your side faces the Sun.

rounds.explain: When our side turns away from the Sun, it is dark, so it is night.

rounds.ask: Does the Moon really change shape?

options.label: yes, it shrinks
options.why: The Moon stays round. We just see less of its sunny side.

rounds.explain: The Moon is always a round ball. We just see different parts of it lit by the Sun.

intro.say: Eight planets travel around the Sun. Let's learn their names and their order, starting closest to the Sun.

rounds.say: The four planets closest to the Sun are small and rocky: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars.
rounds.caption: rocky planets

rounds.say: The next four are giant planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Jupiter is the biggest planet of all!
rounds.caption: giant planets

rounds.ask: Put the rocky planets in order, starting next to the Sun.
rounds.explain: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars. Earth is the third planet from the Sun.
rounds.hint: Mercury is the closest to the Sun.

rounds.ask: Now put the giant planets in order, going away from the Sun.
rounds.explain: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun.

rounds.ask: Which planet is closest to the Sun?

options.label: Earth
options.why: Earth is third. Mercury is first.

options.label: Neptune
options.why: Neptune is the farthest away, not the closest.

rounds.explain: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun.

rounds.ask: Which planet do we live on?

options.label: Mars
options.why: Mars is our neighbor, but no people live there.

options.label: Saturn
options.why: Saturn is a giant planet made of gas.

rounds.explain: We live on Earth, the third planet from the Sun.

options.label: Mercury
options.why: Mercury is the smallest planet.

options.label: Earth
options.why: Earth is small next to the giant planets.

rounds.explain: Jupiter is the biggest planet. More than a thousand Earths could fit inside it!

rounds.ask: Which planet has big, bright rings?

options.label: Mars
options.why: Mars is a red, rocky planet with no big rings.

rounds.explain: Saturn is famous for its big, bright rings made of ice and rock.
